title: Implement cmd/cat concatenate utility (prd006-cat R1-R5)
description:
deliverable_type: code

required_reading:
  - docs/specs/product-requirements/prd006-cat.yaml (all flag behaviors, transformation order, exit codes)
  - docs/ARCHITECTURE.yaml (cmd/ package structure and conventions)
  - go.mod (module path github.com/petar-djukic/go-unix-utils)

files:
  - path: cmd/cat/main.go
    action: create
    note: cat utility -- passthrough, line numbering, blank squeezing, non-printing display, error handling

requirements:
  - id: R1
    text: "Implement default behavior: read named files in order, or stdin when no files are given or '-' is given as a filename; write contents verbatim to stdout; handle binary input (all byte values 0x00-0xFF) without corruption; do not add or remove newlines from the input (prd006-cat R1.1-R1.5)"
  - id: R2
    text: "Implement line-numbering flags -n and -b: -n prepends a right-justified 6-wide line number followed by a tab character to every output line using format '%6d\\t'; -b prepends a number only to non-blank lines, leaving blank lines without a number or tab; -b overrides -n when both are given; a blank line is defined as a line containing only a newline character (prd006-cat R2.1-R2.4)"
  - id: R3
    text: "Implement blank-line squeezing -s: collapse two or more consecutive blank output lines to one; the first blank line is written and subsequent consecutive blank lines are discarded; squeezing applies across file boundaries when multiple files are concatenated; apply squeezing before line numbering so suppressed blank lines do not consume line numbers (prd006-cat R3.1-R3.3)"
  - id: R4
    text: "Implement non-printing display flags -v, -E, -T, -A, -e, -t, -u: -v encodes control characters 0x00-0x1F (except tab 0x09 and newline 0x0A) as ^X where X is 64 positions higher, 0x7F as ^?, and bytes 0x80-0xFF with M- prefix; -E appends '$' before each newline; -T displays tab as '^I'; -A equals -v -E -T combined; -e equals -v -E; -t equals -v -T; -u accepted without effect; apply transformations in order: squeeze blanks, non-printing display, end-of-line marker, line-number prefix (prd006-cat R4.1-R4.9)"
  - id: R5
    text: "Implement error handling and exit codes: exit 0 on success; exit 1 when any input file cannot be opened -- print error message to stderr and continue processing remaining file arguments; exit 1 on stdout write error; do not exit non-zero due to SIGPIPE when stdout is closed by a downstream consumer (prd006-cat R5.1-R5.4)"

design_decisions:
  - id: D1
    text: "Module path is github.com/petar-djukic/go-unix-utils per go.mod; binary entry point is cmd/cat/main.go with package main; no external dependencies beyond the Go standard library"
  - id: D2
    text: "Apply transformations in the fixed order from prd006-cat R4.9: squeeze blanks (-s) first, then non-printing display (-v/-T), then end-of-line marker (-E), then line-number prefix (-n/-b); this order is non-negotiable per the spec"
  - id: D3
    text: "Read input line-by-line using bufio.Reader.ReadBytes('\\n') rather than bufio.Scanner, so that partial last lines (no trailing newline) are preserved without reconstruction; the newline byte (when present) is included in the returned slice and must be preserved in output"
  - id: D4
    text: "Handle SIGPIPE by catching syscall.SIGPIPE via os/signal and calling os.Exit(0) so that piping cat output to head or other truncating consumers exits cleanly without a broken-pipe error message, matching gcat behavior (prd006-cat R5.4)"

acceptance_criteria:
  - id: AC1
    text: "'go build ./cmd/cat/' succeeds with no errors and produces a runnable binary"
  - id: AC2
    text: "Default mode: all 256 byte values (0x00-0xFF) pass through without corruption when no flags are active; output bytes are identical to input bytes"
  - id: AC3
    text: "-n produces format '     N\\t' (6-wide right-justified number followed by tab) for every output line including blank lines; -b produces the same format for non-blank lines only, blank lines receive no number and no tab; -b takes precedence over -n when both are given"
  - id: AC4
    text: "-s with input containing four consecutive blank lines produces exactly one blank line in output; squeezing applies across file boundaries so the last blank line of one file and the first blank line of the next file count as consecutive"
  - id: AC5
    text: "-v encodes: 0x01 as '^A', 0x1B as '^[', 0x7F as '^?', 0x80 as 'M-^@', 0xA0 as 'M- ', 0xFF as 'M-^?'; tab (0x09) and newline (0x0A) are not altered by -v"
  - id: AC6
    text: "-A produces output byte-for-byte identical to applying -v, -E, -T simultaneously; -e produces output identical to -v -E; -t produces output identical to -v -T"
  - id: AC7
    text: "A non-existent file argument causes a descriptive error message on stderr and an exit code of 1; any remaining valid file arguments on the command line are still read and written to stdout before the process exits"

title: Implement pkg/testutils differential testing harness (prd001 R1-R5)
description:
deliverable_type: code

required_reading:
  - docs/specs/product-requirements/prd001-testutils.yaml
  - docs/ARCHITECTURE.yaml (pkg/testutils component section)
  - go.mod (module path for import declarations)

files:
  - path: pkg/testutils/difftest.go
    action: create
    note: DiffTest struct, NormalizeFunc type, RunDiffTests entry point, binary execution, comparison and reporting, file-state comparison
  - path: pkg/testutils/normalizer.go
    action: create
    note: TimestampNormalizer built-in normalizer

requirements:
  - id: R1
    text: "Define the DiffTest struct per prd001 R1.1-R1.4 with fields Args []string, Stdin []byte, Env []string, ExitCode int, Normalizers []NormalizeFunc, FileExpectations []FileExpectation, and WDir string. Define NormalizeFunc as func([]byte) []byte. Define FileExpectation as a struct with Path string and Content []byte. Nil Stdin means immediate EOF; nil Env means the binary inherits the test process environment; nil or empty Normalizers means no normalization is applied."
  - id: R2
    text: "Implement binary execution per prd001 R2.1-R2.5: RunDiffTests(t *testing.T, goBinary string, refBinary string, tests []DiffTest) invokes both binaries with identical Args, Stdin, and Env, captures stdout/stderr/exit code from each independently, imposes a 10-second default timeout (fail with clear timeout message if exceeded), and uses a per-test os.MkdirTemp working directory when DiffTest.WDir is empty."
  - id: R3
    text: "Implement comparison and reporting per prd001 R3.1-R3.6: apply DiffTest.Normalizers in order to both binaries' stdout and stderr before comparison; compare normalized stdout byte-for-byte, normalized stderr byte-for-byte, and exit codes exactly; report divergence with triggering args, stdin truncated to 256 bytes, both stdouts, both stderrs, and both exit codes; run each DiffTest as a t.Run named subtest using the DiffTest index or a name derived from its args."
  - id: R4
    text: "Implement normalization composition per prd001 R4.1-R4.3: the Normalizers slice on DiffTest is applied left-to-right to both binaries' outputs before comparison. Implement TimestampNormalizer in normalizer.go as a NormalizeFunc that replaces strings matching the ts default strftime format '%b %d %H:%M:%S' (e.g. 'Feb 19 14:05:32') with the fixed placeholder 'TIMESTAMP' using a compiled regexp."
  - id: R5
    text: "Implement file-state comparison per prd001 R5.1-R5.2: after both binaries exit, for each FileExpectation in DiffTest.FileExpectations read the file at Path (relative to the test working directory used by that binary's invocation) and compare its content byte-for-byte with FileExpectation.Content, reporting path and both file contents on divergence using the same t.Errorf format as stdout divergence."

design_decisions:
  - id: D1
    text: "Name the primary file difftest.go because the primary exported type is DiffTest, per the project file naming convention (testutils/testutils.go is forbidden)."
  - id: D2
    text: "RunDiffTests signature is RunDiffTests(t *testing.T, goBinary string, refBinary string, tests []DiffTest) per prd001 AC1. The function is the sole public entry point for the harness."
  - id: D3
    text: "The Normalizers field on DiffTest is []NormalizeFunc (a slice, not a single function) per prd001 R4.3. Both binaries' outputs are passed through the same normalizer sequence before byte-for-byte comparison."
  - id: D4
    text: "Use exec.CommandContext with context.WithTimeout for binary invocation per prd001 R2.3. Set the default timeout to 10 seconds via a package-level constant DefaultTimeout = 10 * time.Second. Do not expose a per-test timeout override in this task."
  - id: D5
    text: "Each binary invocation runs in its own subdirectory under the per-test temp directory so that file-state comparisons (prd001 R5) read files written by the correct binary without cross-contamination."

acceptance_criteria:
  - id: AC1
    text: "A caller can define []DiffTest and invoke RunDiffTests(t, goBinaryPath, refBinaryPath, tests) with no other setup, per prd001 AC1."
  - id: AC2
    text: "A passing DiffTest run emits no test output. A failing run prints the triggering args, stdin (truncated to 256 bytes), and both binaries' stdout, stderr, and exit code, per prd001 AC2."
  - id: AC3
    text: "TimestampNormalizer replaces a string matching the ts default format (e.g. 'Feb 19 14:05:32') with 'TIMESTAMP' so that ts differential tests pass despite wall-clock differences, per prd001 AC3."
  - id: AC4
    text: "A DiffTest with a FileExpectation whose expected content differs from what one binary writes causes a test failure reporting the path and both file contents, per prd001 AC4."
  - id: AC5
    text: "A DiffTest whose binary exceeds 10 seconds fails immediately with a clear timeout message and does not hang the test run, per prd001 AC5."
  - id: AC6
    text: "go build ./pkg/testutils/... succeeds and golangci-lint reports no warnings on pkg/testutils/, per prd001 AC6."

title: Implement cmd/ts timestamp utility (prd004-ts R1-R8)
description:
deliverable_type: code

required_reading:
  - docs/specs/product-requirements/prd004-ts.yaml
  - docs/ARCHITECTURE.yaml (cmd/ component, project structure)
  - go.mod (module path: github.com/petar-djukic/go-unix-utils)

files:
  - path: cmd/ts/main.go
    action: create
    note: ts binary -- read stdin line by line and prepend strftime timestamps

requirements:
  - id: R1
    text: "Implement default behavior (prd004-ts R1.1-R1.6): read stdin line by line with bufio.NewReader ReadString, prepend a timestamp formatted with '%b %d %H:%M:%S' and a space before each line, flush stdout after every line, pass through partial last lines without trailing newline, and exit 0 on clean EOF."
  - id: R2
    text: "Implement custom format string (prd004-ts R2.1-R2.4): accept an optional positional argument as a strftime format string; translate standard strftime directives to Go time.Format layout strings; implement ts-specific subsecond extensions %.S (seconds.microseconds), %.s (unix-epoch.microseconds), %.T (HH:MM:SS.microseconds) by formatting the base component then appending '.' and six decimal digits from a single time.Now() call per line."
  - id: R3
    text: "Implement incremental mode (prd004-ts R3.1-R3.4): -i flag timestamps each line with elapsed time since the previous line (first line uses elapsed since start); default format '%H:%M:%S' with UTC for elapsed formatting; -i and -s are mutually exclusive -- print usage error to stderr and exit non-zero if both are given."
  - id: R4
    text: "Implement elapsed-since-start mode (prd004-ts R4.1-R4.3): -s flag timestamps each line with total elapsed time since ts started, monotonically increasing; default format '%H:%M:%S' with UTC for elapsed formatting; overridden by a custom format argument."
  - id: R5
    text: "Implement monotonic clock mode (prd004-ts R5.1-R5.3): -m flag selects time.Now() monotonic reading for all timestamp samples; compatible with all format modes including subsecond extensions; timestamps must not jump backwards."
  - id: R6
    text: "Implement relative-time conversion mode (prd004-ts R6.1-R6.5): -r flag scans each line for recognized timestamp patterns -- syslog ('Jan  5 14:30:00'), ISO-8601 ('2024-01-05T14:30:00.000Z'), RFC 2822 with optional day, lastlog ('Mon Jan  5 14:30') -- and replaces each match with a relative age string (e.g., '15m5s ago'); if a custom format argument is also given, reformat matched timestamps via that strftime format instead; lines without a recognized timestamp pass through unchanged; -r is mutually exclusive with -i and -s."
  - id: R7
    text: "Implement exit codes and error handling (prd004-ts R7.1-R7.3): exit 0 on clean stdin EOF; exit non-zero and print a usage message to stderr for unrecognized flags; handle SIGPIPE by installing a signal handler that calls os.Exit(0) when stdout is closed by a downstream consumer, suppressing broken-pipe errors."
  - id: R8
    text: "Implement TZ environment handling (prd004-ts R8.1-R8.2): honor the TZ environment variable for wall-clock timestamps in default mode by loading the time.Location from the TZ value before formatting; use UTC internally for elapsed timestamp formatting in -i and -s modes regardless of the process TZ setting, matching the TZ=GMT behavior of the Perl source."

design_decisions:
  - id: D1
    text: "Use time.Now() for all clock reads. Go's time.Time automatically carries a monotonic reading, so -m mode requires no special clock selection -- the same call satisfies both wall-clock and monotonic requirements (prd004-ts R5.1)."
  - id: D2
    text: "Implement strftime by translating standard directives (%Y, %m, %d, %H, %M, %S, %b, %j, %p, %Z, %%, etc.) to Go time.Format layout strings before calling Format(). For the three ts subsecond extensions (%.S, %.s, %.T), extract the base component via Format(), then append '.' and fmt.Sprintf('%06d', t.Nanosecond()/1000) for microsecond precision (prd004-ts R2.3)."
  - id: D3
    text: "For -i and -s elapsed timestamps, compute the duration, convert to whole seconds (int64), and call time.Unix(seconds, 0).UTC().Format(layout) to produce the HH:MM:SS string under UTC semantics, matching the TZ=GMT behavior of the Perl source (prd004-ts R3.2, R4.2)."
  - id: D4
    text: "Use bufio.NewReader(os.Stdin) with ReadString('\\n') to read lines. This correctly handles partial last lines (no trailing newline at EOF) and avoids bufio.Scanner's 64 KB default buffer limit (prd004-ts R1.5)."
  - id: D5
    text: "For -r mode, compile the four timestamp regexes once at startup with regexp.MustCompile. Compute relative age as time.Since(parsedTime) and format as '<Xh><Ym><Zs> ago' with only non-zero components shown, except always show seconds (prd004-ts R6.1-R6.2)."

acceptance_criteria:
  - id: AC1
    text: "echo 'hello world' | go run ./cmd/ts produces a line matching '<month> <day> <HH:MM:SS> hello world' using the default '%b %d %H:%M:%S' format (prd004-ts AC1)."
  - id: AC2
    text: "printf 'a\\nb\\nc\\n' | go run ./cmd/ts -s produces three lines with monotonically non-decreasing elapsed timestamps in HH:MM:SS format (prd004-ts AC2)."
  - id: AC3
    text: "go run ./cmd/ts -z (unrecognized flag) prints a usage message to stderr and exits with a non-zero code (prd004-ts AC4)."
  - id: AC4
    text: "go run ./cmd/ts with empty stdin (immediate EOF) produces no output and exits 0 (prd004-ts AC5)."
  - id: AC5
    text: "go run ./cmd/ts -i -s prints a usage error to stderr and exits non-zero (prd004-ts R3.4)."
  - id: AC6
    text: "go run ./cmd/ts -r on input 'Jan  1 00:00:00 boot message' outputs a line where the syslog timestamp is replaced by a relative age string followed by the remaining content (prd004-ts R6.1-R6.2)."
  - id: AC7
    text: "cmd/ts compiles successfully with go build ./cmd/ts/... and produces no warnings under golangci-lint (prd004-ts AC6)."

title: GH-27: Upgrade docs to latest cobbler-scaffold documentation standard
description:
## Description

Upgrade all project documentation to align with the latest cobbler-scaffold documentation standard following a scaffold upgrade to v0.20260227.2.

## Acceptance Criteria

- mage analyze passes with no warnings
- SPECIFICATIONS.yaml and road-map.yaml reflect current project state
- All YAML docs pass forbidden-term and writing-style audit
- YAML docs use title/content section structure for markdown-convertibility
- README matches readme-format.md standard
- All engineering guidelines and use cases have all required fields per design.yaml

GitHub: petar-djukic/go-unix-utils#27

title: Investigate and resolve mage analyze multi-release PRD warnings
description:
## Required Reading

- configuration.yaml
- docs/road-map.yaml
- docs/specs/product-requirements/prd001-testutils.yaml
- docs/specs/product-requirements/prd002-sys.yaml
- docs/specs/product-requirements/prd003-format.yaml
- All docs/specs/use-cases/*.yaml (for touchpoint references)
- docs/constitutions/design.yaml (traceability model, PRD format)

## Files to Modify

TBD after investigation. Likely one or more of: configuration.yaml, use case touchpoints, road-map.yaml, or SPECIFICATIONS.yaml.

## Requirements

mage analyze currently warns that prd001-testutils, prd002-sys, and prd003-format span releases 01.0 through 02.1. These are shared-library PRDs used by utility use cases across all releases. The check "each PRD must belong to exactly one release" was introduced in cobbler-scaffold v0.20260227.2.

Determine the correct resolution: (a) add a shared_prds exclusion to configuration.yaml if the orchestrator supports it, (b) remove PRD ID references from use case touchpoints (touchpoints should reference architectural components, not PRD IDs), or (c) add a shared: true marker to these PRDs. Implement the resolution and verify mage analyze exits 0 with no warnings.

## Acceptance Criteria

- mage analyze exits 0 with no warnings
- Traceability from shared-library components to use cases is preserved in some form
- The resolution is documented in a brief note in ARCHITECTURE.yaml or configuration.yaml

title: Audit all YAML docs for forbidden terms, writing style, and title/content section structure
description:
## Required Reading

- docs/VISION.yaml
- docs/ARCHITECTURE.yaml
- docs/SPECIFICATIONS.yaml
- docs/road-map.yaml
- All docs/specs/product-requirements/prd*.yaml
- All docs/specs/use-cases/*.yaml
- All docs/specs/test-suites/*.yaml
- All docs/engineering/eng*.yaml
- docs/constitutions/design.yaml (documentation_standards section)

## Files to Modify

Any YAML doc containing violations.

## Requirements

Audit all YAML docs against the documentation_standards from design.yaml:

Forbidden terms: critical, critically, key, deliberate, strategic, precisely, absolutely, fundamental, breakthrough, principled, honest, at the heart of, grounded, standards-aligned. Remove or replace every occurrence.

Writing style: Use the royal "we" in active voice. Flag and fix any passive voice or third-person constructions (e.g., "This document describes..." or "The architecture implements...").

Formatting: No bold text (**text**) in prose. No horizontal rules. Tables instead of lists for short entries. No colons in prose except to introduce lists.

Section structure for markdown conversion: The cobbler-scaffold standard expects YAML sections to use title/content keys (as engineering guidelines already do) so they can be converted to markdown for display. Audit all multi-section documents to verify they use this structure or a compatible one, and update any that do not.

## Acceptance Criteria

- No forbidden terms remain in any doc under docs/
- All prose uses "we" in active voice
- No bold text or horizontal rules appear in multi-line string fields
- Sections use title/content keys where applicable

title: Audit README against latest readme-format.md standard
description:
## Required Reading

- README.md
- docs/VISION.yaml (for authoritative scope and status numbers)
- docs/ARCHITECTURE.yaml

## Files to Modify

- README.md

## Requirements

Audit README.md against the readme-format.md standard from cobbler-scaffold:

Section order: Title + one-line description, architectural thesis, system diagram (Mermaid), project scope and status (concrete numbers), methodology, repository structure, technology choices, build and test instructions. Extra sections (Tagging Scheme, Documentation) may follow but must not precede the standard eight.

Writing style: Active voice, present tense. "We implement" not "We have implemented." No buzzwords. No emoji. No bold in headers or body text. No keyword stuffing.

Content accuracy: Scope and status numbers must be current. Technology choices must include rationale ("Go because X"). Repository structure tree must match actual layout.

Prose quality: Each section must read as a technical brief, not a sales pitch or tutorial. The thesis (first 3 sections) must stand alone for a 30-second scan.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Sections are in the order specified by readme-format.md
- All prose is present tense and uses "we" or passive where appropriate for technical documentation
- Scope/status table numbers match current project state
- No buzzwords, emoji, or bold text remain

title: Audit engineering guidelines and use cases for field completeness against design.yaml
description:
## Required Reading

- docs/constitutions/design.yaml (completeness_checklists, document_types sections)
- All docs/engineering/eng*.yaml
- All docs/specs/use-cases/*.yaml
- All docs/specs/test-suites/*.yaml

## Files to Modify

Any file missing required fields.

## Requirements

Engineering guidelines (eng*.yaml) must have: id, title, introduction, sections (list with title and content), and optionally references. Verify eng01 through eng09 all conform. Pay particular attention to newer guidelines (eng07, eng08, eng09) which may have been written under earlier standards.

Use cases must have: id, title, summary, actor, trigger, flow (F1, F2, ...), touchpoints (T1, T2, ...), success_criteria (S1, S2, ...), out_of_scope, test_suite. Verify all 7 use cases conform. Touchpoints should reference architecture components; PRD IDs may appear as parenthetical context but must not be the primary reference.

Test suites must have: id, title, release, traces, test_cases with name/inputs/expected outputs per case. Verify all 4 test suite files conform.

## Acceptance Criteria

- All eng*.yaml files have required fields with no missing sections
- All use case YAML files have required fields with correct numbering (F1..., T1..., S1...)
- All test suite YAML files have required fields
- mage analyze exits clean after any changes
